claims.claim: The librarian skill was not available in this run, so the existing-knowledge check could not retrieve artifacts
claims.evidence: Stated consistently in the Existing Knowledge section and footer; no transcript available to contradict, and behavior (suggesting searches instead of running them) is consistent with the claim.

claims.claim: The opening clarifying question was self-answered because the run was non-interactive
claims.evidence: opening-question.md contains the standalone question, and notification-system.md's assumptions note (lines 5-9) explains the self-answer, which is consistent with a single-shot eval harness.

claims.claim: 8 distinct capabilities cover the standard-depth notification system
claims.evidence: Counted CAP-01 through CAP-08, each with Trigger/Inputs/Logic flow/Outputs/Edge cases/Connects to, and reflected in the Dependency Map.

suggestions.assertion: Checks for existing knowledge via librarian skill before starting
suggestions.reason: In this run the librarian skill was unavailable, so the assertion passes on an intent statement ('an agent with librarian access should check') rather than an actual tool invocation. The assertion cannot distinguish a genuine librarian query from a graceful fallback note. Consider asserting on an observable librarian tool call when the skill is available, or explicitly scoping this assertion to the fallback behavior.

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT immediately produce a final document — engages in dialogue first
suggestions.reason: In a non-interactive harness there is no real dialogue; the skill self-answers its own question and writes the final document in the same run. This assertion passes based on the separate opening-question.md artifact + an assumptions note rather than observed multi-turn dialogue. Consider verifying via transcript turn count when interactive, since a skill could fabricate the dialogue framing without truly pausing for input.

eval_feedback.overall: Document-structure and content assertions are strong and discriminating. The two interactive/process assertions (librarian check, dialogue-first) are weaker under a non-interactive harness because they pass on stated intent rather than observed runtime behavior; worth tightening when the skill runs with tools available and a transcript to inspect.
